scenes.say: Ever get a merge conflict in Git? What do you actually do when it happens?

scenes.label: Real-life
scenes.sub: Interviewers want to see you handle conflicts.
scenes.say: Interviewers want to see if you can handle real-life code conflicts, just like in a real team.

scenes.title: Conflict markers
scenes.say: When changes overlap, Git marks the file and shows conflict markers. You’ll see these arrows and equals signs in your code.
Here’s how to fix it: Open the file, find the markers, edit and combine the code, remove the markers, then stage and commit.

scenes.question: What’s a common mistake when resolving?
scenes.right: You must edit the code to keep the right changes, not just delete the markers.
scenes.say: A common mistake is just deleting the markers. You have to actually edit and combine the code to keep the right changes.
